transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-01 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Thompson, Daniel Park (Redwood); Laura Chen, Ravi Patel, Sofia Martinez, Ethan Brooks (Aurelia)

Summary:
Quick procurement and legal walkthrough to confirm MSA/DPA windows, SLA expectations, KMS/SSO requirements, and next steps for pilot billing clearance. SE to propose technical preflight and connectivity checklist. Legal to produce redlines. Pricing to be circulated for committee approval.

Topics:
- MSA/DPA high-level exceptions
- Encryption & BYOK/KMS options
- Data residency and EU export controls
- SLA tiers and uptime/credits
- Billing model: hosted vs dedicated economics and egress assumptions
- Onboarding timeline and pilot SOW

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Thompson: Hey everyone thanks for joining - looks like we have most folks here, um we can start. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Laura Chen: Laura here - procurement.
[00:11] Ravi Patel: Ravi, CISO.
[00:13] Sofia Martinez: Sofia, legal.
[00:15] Ethan Brooks: Ethan, infra.
[00:17] Daniel Park: Daniel from Redwood, hey all.
[00:20] Maya Thompson: Cool. High level agenda, we want to make sure the MSA/DPA alignment is clear, go over SLA and KMS/SSO pathing, then cover the pilot pricing and next steps.
[00:32] Laura Chen: We're on a fairly tight procurement cadence, um our vendor committee meets on the 12th, so we need commercial terms cleared by then ideally.
[00:38] Maya Thompson: Understood - is the 12th the final approval gate or is there an earlier finance committee?
[00:43] Laura Chen: That's the fiscal gate for approval. We need commercial, legal and security thumbs up before then.
[00:47] Maya Thompson: Great. Ravi, maybe start with security priorities for Aurelia so we can align on the DPA/MSA asks?
[00:53] Ravi Patel: Sure. Primary is BYOK or at least customer-managed KMS option for production PII and PHI, we have to lock keys. Also audit logs with at least 1 year retention and ability to export logs to our SIEM. SOC2 is fine but we also want proof of encryption at rest with our key.
[01:12] Daniel Park: Quick note - Redwood Private supports BYOK in the private deployment and Dedicated has a bring-your-own-key option, yeah. For hosted we have envelope encryption and a KMS integration pathway but full BYOK requires Private.
[01:26] Ravi Patel: Okay. We may need a hybrid: pilot on Redwood Hosted with customer-managed envelope keys for the first phase, then Dedicated or Private for production.
[01:35] Maya Thompson: That sequence makes sense. For the DPA redlines, Sofia, any initial items?
[01:40] Sofia Martinez: Indemnity language, sub-processing, and data deletion timelines - 30 days seems tight for us but we can discuss. Also we have to check data residency clauses - Aurelia requires EU data to remain in EU regions and not be processed in the US without explicit consent.
[01:56] Maya Thompson: Redwood supports regional routing for requests by policy, but I want to be clear that model variant fallback across regions is a complex area - you'll see that in the DPA wording.
[02:09] Ethan Brooks: Are there any egress fees? Our cloud team is sensitive to hidden egress or cross-region transfer costs.
[02:16] Daniel Park: Pricing-wise, hosted includes standard egress to the same region; cross-region transfers incur a small fee. For Dedicated we can negotiate network egress terms as part of the reserved capacity contract. We'll put numbers in the commercial term sheet.
[02:30] Laura Chen: On SSO - we use Okta, must have SAML SSO plus SCIM for provisioning. Also RBAC is required for 5 different roles.
[02:38] Daniel Park: Redwood Console supports SAML & SCIM. RBAC is configurable and we can provide a mapping doc.
[02:44] Sofia Martinez: On SLA, our baseline expectation is 99.95 for production and clear crediting for downtime. What are Redwood's standard SLA tiers?
[02:52] Maya Thompson: Typical baseline is 99.9 for hosted with a premium 99.95 for Dedicated under an SLA addendum. Credits scale by outage minutes. We can surface specifics in the SLA addendum.
[03:05] Ravi Patel: We will need a runbook and post-incident report obligations in the MSA.
[03:10] Maya Thompson: Absolutely, post-incident reports for severity 1 incidents are standard and included in the incident response section.
[03:15] Daniel Park: Also to call out - graceful degradation: model variant fallbacks, and a documented fallback to smaller quantized variants. That's operational and we can include language in the SLO appendix.
[03:29] Ethan Brooks: From infra perspective - port ranges, IP allowlist, and VPN support for Private deployments. We need a connectivity checklist.
[03:37] Daniel Park: We'll provide an endpoint connectivity checklist. For Private, we support VPC peering and on-prem agents.
[03:43] Laura Chen: Commercial: we generally prefer a 12-month pilot with a small committed spend that converts to reserved capacity if successful. Pricing approvals need to be presented to FinOps with clear unit economics.
[03:55] Maya Thompson: For pilots we offer a 30-90 day evaluation plus pilot credits, and a canonical pilot SOW. If you want a 12-month pilot that's fine and we can present commit tiers with step-ups.
[04:07] Sofia Martinez: Any escrow or code escrow for model weights? We're in pharma and there's some IP sensitivity.
[04:13] Daniel Park: We don't escrow open model weights typically; if there's a special requirement we can escalate for an enterprise agreement.
[04:19] Ravi Patel: Another ask - vulnerability disclosure and patch cadence documentation, we need that for the security questionnaire.
[04:25] Daniel Park: We'll share our patch cadence doc and vulnerability disclosure policy in the security packet.
[04:30] Maya Thompson: Ok so to summarize the main outstanding redlines: KMS/BYOK options, data residency and export controls, SLA 99.95 vs 99.9, incident runbooks, indemnity language, and commercial commit levels. Anything else?
[04:44] Sofia Martinez: Export control clause for EU data, and also subprocessor list or at least a commitment to provide list on request.
[04:51] Daniel Park: We maintain a subprocessors list and can provide updates in the DPA.
[04:55] Laura Chen: One other operational ask - we need the invoice cadence to be monthly and a PO number mapping. Also any early termination fees should be clear.
[05:05] Maya Thompson: We'll make sure billing cadence and PO mapping are explicit in the SOW; early termination terms are negotiable in the reserved capacity addendum.
[05:12] Ethan Brooks: On benchmarking: we want to run performance tests against our expected latency SLOs - can Redwood provide a test harness and a short benchmark plan?
[05:21] Daniel Park: Yes, SE can share a benchmark plan and a small load harness to run on your side. We typically do synthetic latency tests and a token-cost estimate sheet.
[05:33] Maya Thompson: Let's talk timeline - procurement meeting on the 12th means legal needs redlines early next week. Sofia, is 2025-11-08 a workable date to get initial redlines?
[05:43] Sofia Martinez: Yes we'll aim for the 8th but may have follow-ups.
[05:47] Maya Thompson: Great. On pricing - I'll walk through a rough structure now: pilot credits for 60 days, then if you convert to reserved capacity we propose a tiered commit with a 10-20% discount vs pay-as-you-go; Dedicated has a different pricing sheet with fixed monthly fees and optional burst.
[06:07] Laura Chen: Will that require an escrow or financial guarantee? Our finance team sometimes asks for an invoice holdback on pilots.
[06:15] Maya Thompson: Pilot invoices tend to be minimal; for reserved capacity we have contract terms and deposit options. We can model options in the term sheet.
[06:24] Ethan Brooks: Network security — we will need TLS mutual auth for service-to-service if we connect over private network.
[06:31] Daniel Park: Mutual TLS is supported in Private and we can configure client certs.
[06:36] Ravi Patel: Anything about data classification - PHI, PII? We have samples that will be PHI; is Redwood validated for HIPAA?
[06:44] Maya Thompson: Redwood itself maintains SOC2 and can support HIPAA on a case-by-case basis with a BA agreement. We can scope that with legal.
[06:54] Sofia Martinez: Ok, we'll flag HIPAA requirement if that pilot will include PHI.
[06:59] Maya Thompson: Good. Any questions from Aurelia side about model weights or fine-tuning?
[07:05] Ethan Brooks: We plan to fine-tune on internal prompts. Is fine-tuning supported in hosted? Does it require dedicated infra?
[07:12] Daniel Park: Fine-tuning pipelines are supported but for customer-private data we recommend Private or Dedicated to avoid cross-tenant exposure. We'll include that guidance in the tech preflight doc.
[07:22] Laura Chen: On DPA deletion timelines - 30 days is aggressive, 90 days is more realistic. What's Redwood's standard?
[07:30] Maya Thompson: Standard is 45-60 days for full purge across backups; we can negotiate to 30 for certain classes with a Private deployment.
[07:39] Ravi Patel: For audibility we also require that deletion triggers are logged and a certificate of deletion is provided.
[07:46] Daniel Park: We can provide deletion receipts for production if that's a firm requirement.
[07:51] Maya Thompson: Switching to an operational note — we'll put together an onboarding playbook that includes connectivity, SSO, RBAC, billing, and security artifacts. That's part of the pilot SOW.
[08:03] Ethan Brooks: Can you share the onboarding playbook prior to our infra deep-dive?
[08:08] Daniel Park: Yes, SE will attach the playbook and a short connectivity checklist.
[08:12] Maya Thompson: Quick check on pilot scope: are you expecting embeddings, chat endpoints, or both?
[08:18] Ethan Brooks: Both — the primary use is clinical Q&A embeddings + a triage chat assistant.
[08:25] Daniel Park: Ok we'll note workloads and advise on quantization/throughput versus latency tradeoffs.
[08:33] Laura Chen: On legal cycles - if we get redlines on the 8th and Redwood responds the 10th, can we realistically get committee sign-off by the 12th? That is a tight turnaround.
[08:43] Maya Thompson: We'll prioritize the redlines and offer to be on a quick call with your legal if needed the 11th.
[08:50] Sofia Martinez: That help would be useful.
[08:53] Maya Thompson: Alright I'll propose the 11th for a short legal readout if you want.
[08:59] Daniel Park: We'll also include a short appendix for SLA credit calculation and severity definitions to make the review faster.
[09:07] Ravi Patel: About support — what is the support SLA and escalation path for Dedicated customers?
[09:14] Maya Thompson: Dedicated customers get 24/7 on-call with a named escalation engineer and guaranteed response times in the SLA addendum. Hosted has standard support hours with optional premium support.
[09:26] Laura Chen: Our procurement will want to know named contacts for escalation and an NDA is already in place?
[09:32] Maya Thompson: We can provide named contacts post-signature but can provide role-based escalation windows now. NDA - if you have one we can sign; we have a standard mutual NDA as well.
[09:42] Ethan Brooks: Any compliance certifications beyond SOC2? ISO 27001?
[09:46] Daniel Park: We have SOC2 and are pursuing ISO; we'll include a timeline in the packet.
[09:52] Sofia Martinez: Slight aside - indemnity caps are often a sticking point for our legal. Can Redwood provide examples of previous indemnity clauses or a standard approach?
[09:59] Maya Thompson: We'll include sample indemnity language; many customers request a $X million cap depending on tier. We'll flag that in the commercial term sheet.
[10:09] Laura Chen: Great. For the purchase order mechanics: we want monthly invoices tied to a single PO with line items for reserved capacity and overages.
[10:18] Maya Thompson: Noted. We'll provide a mock invoice template showing PO mapping and line items.
[10:25] Daniel Park: Technical note: for the benchmark, we'll need a small list of sample prompts and expected latency targets; also whether you accept synthetic load or prefer replaying production traces.
[10:37] Ethan Brooks: We'll provide sanitized traces for the bench.
[10:41] Maya Thompson: Perfect. On pilot duration—you mentioned 12 months earlier; do you want to structure that as a 90-day initial evaluation then stepped commit?
[10:50] Laura Chen: Yes, a stepped commit works for finance approvals.
[10:54] Maya Thompson: Alright. Any last-open items before we wrap?
[10:57] Ravi Patel: Just to reiterate BYOK and deletion receipts as must-haves for production.
[11:03] Maya Thompson: Noted. We'll highlight those as non-negotiables vs negotiable items.
[11:09] Sofia Martinez: We'll aim to circulate redlines the 8th.
[11:12] Maya Thompson: Thanks everyone. I'll recap next steps and circulate notes.

Recap (verbatim):
- Redwood to send security packet (SOC2 summary, KMS whitepaper, patch cadence)
- SE to send connectivity checklist and benchmark plan
- AE to circulate pricing tiers, pilot SOW, and sample invoices
- Aurelia to return MSA/DPA redlines by 2025-11-08
- Schedule legal readout call on 2025-11-11 if needed
